messages:
samir.support: Customer (tenant-acme-42) hitting intermittent 504s on hosted API starting ~09:12. They say ~10% of requests time out. Sample curl they used attached. Can ops/eng triage?
cheng.eng: Looking at gateway traces — seeing long dequeue waits and batcher backlog around the same window. gateway log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-17T09:12:34Z] tenant=tenant-acme-42 request_id=abc123 gateway.deque_wait=630ms batcher.queue_depth=1207 max_queue_depth=1024 evict_count=0
[2026-03-17T09:12:35Z] request=... status=504 route=hosted-model-a latency=750ms
```
Seems like queue depth exceeded configured max and requests hit the tail timeout.
samir.support: I have the customer's curl repro (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-customer' -d '{"model":"hosted-model-a","input":"<long chat history>... repeated messages","max_tokens":512}'
```
They mentioned these are batched bulk calls from their ingestion pipeline (bursty).
evelyn.sre: @cheng.eng can you confirm whether continuous-batcher paused or got slow kvcache misses? I see a lot of K/V cache churn in the same timeframe.
cheng.eng: KVCACHE hitrate dropped, and eviction pressure spiked. Relevant trace: 
```
batcher: collect_candidates -> seq_len=2048 batching_group=longseq
kvcache.miss=0.43 evictions=312 queue_depth=1207
continuous_batcher: flush_delay=100ms -> actual_flush=430ms
```
When flush_delay balloons the effective latency SLO is violated and gateway times out.
oncall-lucas: Pinging oncall to consider temporary mitigations: 1) apply tenant soft-rate-limit 2) enable per-tenant small-batch routing 3) increase batcher max_depth for short window. Which is safest?
evelyn.sre: Agreed. Immediate actions we did: applied temporary tenant throttle (0.6x), enabled fallback to hosted-model-b (shorter seq optimized), and increased continuous-batcher max_queue_depth from 1024 -> 2048 for 5 minutes while draining. Noted customers saw reduced 504s.
samir.support: Customer confirmed error rate dropped after your changes but wants root cause / permanent fix. They also flagged billing spikes because retries increased.
cheng.eng: Root cause summary for ticket: tenant microburst of long-sequence requests caused continuous-batcher flush delays due to heavy KV cache churn and oversized groupings. Queue depth exceeded configured limit -> tail timeouts (504). Replay steps for eng: 
1) repro locally with a busy loop sending long-seq requests (seq_len ~1800-2048) at 800 rps against a single tenant.
2) Observe batcher.queue_depth climbing past 1k and flush_delay -> 400ms+
3) Check kvcache metrics: miss rate increases, evictions spike.

Repro command (internal):
```bash
python tests/repro/run_microburst.py --tenant tenant-acme-42 --seq-len 2000 --rps 800 --duration 120
```
cheng.eng: Suggested long-term mitigations: - implement adaptive batch shaping to split long-seq into smaller sub-batches for continuous batching - add early-prefetch kvcache warming for tenants with long contexts - per-tenant ingress smoothing + throttles tied to queue depth metrics - better alerting rule: batcher.queue_depth > 800 for 30s -> paged alert
evelyn.sre: Also recommend adding a circuit-breaker fallback: when queue_depth > 1024 route new requests to smaller-model variants or dedicated heavy-tenant pools. We'll add a runbook entry for customer-facing communication.
oncall-lucas: I've created incident PR with timeline and added to runbook: https://redwood.internal/incidents/8643219876 (internal link). Tagging @ops-bot to keep watch. :eyes:
ops-bot: incident-watch created for 8643219876. Monitoring rules applied: batcher.max_depth override -> 2048 (5m), tenant-soft-throttle tenant-acme-42=0.6.
samir.support: Adding customer notes and billing mitigation: advised customer to reduce retries, enabled server-side retry-backoff guidance, and offered a one-time credit for retry costs. They asked for ETA on the adaptive batch shaping change.
cheng.eng: ETA for engineering change ~2 sprints to implement safe batching split + kvcache warm. I'll start a design doc and link it here.
samir.support: Thanks everyone — closing interim escalation. Will follow up with the customer once we have the design doc link and timeline. :thumbsup:
